questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with multiple comorbidities is admitted to a hospital ward where an outbreak of MRSA has been reported. As part of the infection control team, you are tasked with implementing the most effective measure to control the spread of MRSA. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step?
questions.stemHtml: A 60-year-old man with multiple comorbidities is admitted to a hospital ward where an outbreak of MRSA has been reported. As part of the infection control team, you are tasked with implementing the most effective measure to control the spread of MRSA. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step?

options.label: A
options.text: Prophylactic administration of vancomycin to all patients

options.label: C
options.text: Mandating the use of masks before invasive procedures

options.label: D
options.text: Ensuring rigorous hand hygiene before and after patient contact

questions.stem: A 20-year-old college student presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of high fever, rash, and hypotension. She is diagnosed with toxic shock syndrome. The attending physician explains to the medical students that a specific pathogen's toxin, acting as a superantigen, is likely responsible for this clinical presentation. Which organism is most commonly associated with producing superantigens?
questions.stemHtml: A 20-year-old college student presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of high fever, rash, and hypotension. She is diagnosed with toxic shock syndrome. The attending physician explains to the medical students that a specific pathogen's toxin, acting as a superantigen, is likely responsible for this clinical presentation. Which organism is most commonly associated with producing superantigens?

options.label: A
options.text: Staphylococcus aureus, known for causing toxic shock syndrome.

options.label: B
options.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae, a common cause of pneumonia.

options.label: C
options.text: Pseudomonas, often associated with hospital-acquired infections.

options.label: D
options.text: Clostridium, known for causing tetanus and botulism.
